brief.topic: An Equal Angle with an Unequal Secret

s01: A line shares this angle equally.
But it does not usually share the opposite side equally.
Look at the two colored triangles.
With their bases along the bottom, they have the same height.
Their areas therefore follow the ratio of B D to D C.
Now use the two outer sides as bases instead.
Drop a perpendicular from D to each one.
The small right triangles share A D and the same angle at A.
So these two perpendicular heights are equal too.
The same two areas now follow the ratio of A B to A C.
One area comparison has given us two length ratios.
Move the top corner and keep its angle split equally.
The base division changes with the outer sides.
Equal angles reveal a proportion, even when the shape is uneven.

scenes.narration:
A line shares this angle equally. But it does not usually share the opposite side equally.

Call the meeting point D. Look at the two colored triangles. With their bases along the bottom, they have the same height. Their areas therefore follow the ratio of B D to D C.

Now use the two outer sides as bases instead. Drop a perpendicular from D to each one. The small right triangles share A D and the same angle at A. So these two perpendicular heights are equal too.

The same two areas now follow the ratio of A B to A C. One area comparison has given us two length ratios. They must be the same.

Move the top corner and keep its angle split equally. The base division changes with the outer sides. Equal angles reveal a proportion, even when the shape is uneven.
